reachable: Not reachable at the scored position, by construction and by inspection — and that is correct for this axis. `make_batcher` is called exactly once inside `H._train` on `fit_stripped` (the training split) and its `next_batch` returns only integer sequence indices; nothing in the module is imported or invoked by cups_probe/cups_ca. The mv parse, the observation projection and the distinctness filter all run once during setup over cached TRAINING observations and never at a scored read. Gradient path in training is real: batch composition changes the flattened row set every step, which changes both the cross-fit ridge nuisance and the listwise/ring negative pool — I confirmed the composition genuinely differs from uniform (9.0x same-anchor-command pair concentration, median in-batch replicate group 19). Two things to record for the archive rather than as defects: (1) the depth tilt concentrates anchor picks on the deepest chains — the top-15 anchors at full alpha are all depth-7/8 destination reads — while the eligible scored slice is depths 3 and 4 only, so the training pressure sits off the eligible band; (2) the parent's edge (+0.0225) is at the measured noise floor (0.0227), so a single three-seed draw cannot separate this child from its parent regardless of what the mechanism does.
solves_outside_model: No — the boundary is respected. The mv-reachability parse and the observation-distinctness filter are used only to choose WHICH SEQUENCES enter a batch and with whom; the resolved routing never touches the model's input. The return value is `list[int]`. The one part gated on observations being present (`_anchor_stats`, `_reference_scale`) reads `fit[i]["z_obs"]` during setup on the training split only, and the harness never calls the batcher at scoring time. Verified by reading every call site of `G.load_batcher` and by confirming the returned object is a closure over precomputed index tensors. No analogue of the retracted stream shortcut: the batcher cannot stamp anything into a token, and the coded command token it exploits (bit-equal across a matched block) is produced by the stream axis, unchanged from the parent. The paired-difference cancellation is untouched — the batcher installs no predictor keyed on the read location or on move-order position.
summary: The batcher is contract-clean and the mechanism it implements is the mechanism its DESCRIPTION states. Executed against the real 2304-sequence training split: `_route_depth` is bit-identical to the parent's depth vector on every sequence; the distinctness filter keeps 98 of 696 candidates and removes every `mv` and every `>>` command as claimed; matched rows carry a bit-equal command input (max deviation 0.0 in both `z_cmd` and the r4-coded token) with all-distinct targets; the r3_fwl ridge assigns bit-identical fitted values to identical-command rows within a parity half; the block delivers a measured 9.0x concentration of same-anchor-command pairs. Determinism, seed sensitivity, private generator, non-mutation and len/bounds all hold; setup costs 0.12 s; the full genome trains end-to-end. Two claims fail against the code. First, the only empirical statement in the hypothesis — that the route-touched anchors on the real training sample are the two named cups exposure reads at route fractions 0.67 and 1.00 — is wrong twice: those commands occur in ~24.8% of the real split and are excluded by the candidate's own max_rate=0.05, and the quoted figures come from a 24-sequence jail sample where they are below min_occ and are not anchors either. Second, and more load-bearing, the design's stated rationale — that under uniform sampling the ridge fits per-row targets nearly exactly and leaves a small residual, which the matched block is what rescues — is measured false: the cross-fit ridge R^2 is 0.36-0.39 under uniform, the anchor-row residual already retains ~70% of target energy, and the block does not systematically raise it (0.686 vs 0.707 mean over five paired batches, sign flipping). The real, verified effect is a 9x concentration of hard same-command negatives in the listwise/ring term, not a rescued orthogonalization residual. The realized block size is 17, not the claimed 24. Nothing here is a leak or a metric-gaming shape; the outside-the-model line is clean.

divergences.claim: "On the real training sample the route-touched anchors are exactly the cups exposure reads (`cat /tmp/w/cups/etc/cron.d/backup.job`, route fraction 0.67; `cat /tmp/w/cups/var/spool/mail/root.msg`, 1.00), i.e. the contents that a chain of moves later relocates, so the replicate pressure lands on the arm the objective measures."
divergences.what_the_code_does: On the real training split (2304 sequences after split_train_dev) BOTH named commands are structurally EXCLUDED from ever becoming anchors: they occur in 568/2304 (24.7%) and 572/2304 (24.8%) of sequences, versus the candidate's own max_rate=0.05 ceiling of 115. Their real route fractions are 0.621 and 0.645, not 0.67 and 1.00. The quoted numbers reproduce exactly on evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl (24 sequences, 6 occurrences each) — where those commands are ALSO not anchors, being below min_occ=8. So the one empirical statement about where the mechanism lands is wrong on the real split, and was never true of an anchor even in the sample it was taken from. Mitigating: the anchors that actually survive are on-target anyway — at full alpha, 99.1% of anchor pick probability sits on route-touched reads, and the top-15 picks are all post-move destination reads (`cat /tmp/w/cups/etc/nginx/nginx.conf.7`, `cat .../root.msg.8`, ...) at route fraction 1.00. Weight mass: 79% cups paths, 20% cvar.
divergences.evidence: _index_split(fit) on the standardized train split: occ('cat /tmp/w/cups/etc/cron.d/backup.job')=568 rf=0.6215; occ('cat /tmp/w/cups/var/spool/mail/root.msg')=572 rf=0.6451; anchor window [lo=8, hi=115] -> both False. Same parse over the 24-seq jail sample: occ=6/6, rf=0.667/1.000, lo=hi=8 -> both excluded. Realized anchor distribution at alpha=2.5: prob mass on route>0 anchors = 0.9912.

divergences.claim: "Under uniform or image-blocked sampling a given command string appears about once per batch, the 769-dimensional ridge basis can fit the per-row target nearly exactly, the residual it leaves is small and the negatives it manufactures are weak. The matched replicate block supplies precisely the missing design ... the residual it leaves is the content identity itself." This is the load-bearing rationale for the whole candidate.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Measured on real batches through the actual objective code: the cross-fit ridge is nowhere near saturated under uniform sampling (R^2 = 0.357-0.394 on three uniform batches), and the residual it leaves is not small — at anchor-command rows the relative residual energy ||tgt-0.9*fitted||^2/||tgt||^2 is 0.67-0.76 under uniform. Worse, the matched block does not systematically raise it: over five paired batches the batcher's anchor-row residual ratio averages 0.686 versus uniform 0.707, with the sign flipping batch to batch (0.754/0.738/0.613/0.662/0.666 vs 0.683/0.669/0.732/0.687/0.765). The premise that the ridge nearly interpolates and the block rescues the residual is quantitatively false. What the block demonstrably DOES supply is 9.0x concentration of same-anchor-command row pairs, i.e. hard listwise/ring negatives with bit-identical command inputs and distinct targets — a real effect, but not the one the hypothesis argues from.
divergences.evidence: Ran evolve.chunks.objective.r3_fwl._crossfit_nuisance on batches built by r4_pathslot_dualaddress_code.collate from this batcher's indices vs uniform indices, 64 seqs each (~1900 flattened cmd rows). crossfit R2: batcher 0.357/0.369/0.497, uniform 0.380/0.394/0.372. Anchor-row res/tgt across five paired steps as listed. Same-anchor-command pairs over 200 full-ramp batches: batcher 55481, uniform 6149 (ratio 9.02).

divergences.claim: "at bs 64, m 24 and max_rate 0.05 the block is a multiple-of-five gain" and "48 of 64 rows come from at most two groups at full ramp".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The 9x pair gain holds. The m=24 block size largely does not: only 37 of 98 kept anchors have a pool >= 24, and at full alpha only 16.2% of anchor pick probability lands on such a pool. Expected realized block size is 17.0, and the median in-batch maximum replicate group over 200 full-ramp batches is 19 (mean 19.3). tilted_distinct then pads the shortfall with uniform draws, so the realized structure is roughly 34 of 64 rows from two groups plus uniform filler, not 48. The hypothesis discloses this as failure mode 2, so the degradation is honest, but the headline arithmetic in claim (c) is not what runs.
divergences.evidence: kept anchors 98; pools>=24: 37; anchor pick prob mass with pool>=24 = 0.162; sum_k p_k*min(24,|pool_k|) = 16.96; per-batch max replicate group over 200 batches: mean 19.3, median 19, max 38.

divergences.claim: "at `distinct_min` 0.85 it also removes commands whose answer is a function of the IMAGE only (`ls -1 /` has one answer per image ...), which would put pressure on system identity rather than content identity."
divergences.what_the_code_does: `ls -1 /` is removed by max_rate (it occurs in all 2304 sequences), not by the distinctness filter — the filter never sees it. Commands of exactly the class the claim says are removed do survive: `ls -1 /tmp/w/cvar/m3/a` (frac 0.885), `ls /usr/lib` (0.884), `ls -1 /tmp/w/cvar/m4/a` (0.933) and `cat /etc/hostname` (0.850), all at route fraction 0.0. Their pick probability at full alpha is negligible (0.9% of mass sits on all route-0 anchors combined), so the practical impact is small.
divergences.evidence: kept-anchor verb counts: cat 95, ls 3; the four listed image-identity anchors appear in the kept list with route fraction 0.0; prob mass on route>0 anchors = 0.9912.

divergences.claim: "Anchor weight is ... a bonus for anchors whose path is touched by an mv edge in the same sequence."
divergences.what_the_code_does: In `_index_split` the touched set is built from the mv edges themselves, so every `mv A B` command is route-touched by construction — the flag is a tautology for the mv class and carries no information there. It is harmless in practice only because the distinctness filter removes every mv anchor (0 of 98 kept). Worth recording because if the distinctness threshold were ever loosened, the route bonus would preferentially promote mv commands whose observation is constant.
divergences.evidence: _index_split: touched = {src, dst for each mv edge}; the flag loop tests tokens of the command itself, so for parsed[t] = ['mv', A, B] the test hits on A immediately. Measured: route fraction 1.00 for every mv candidate; kept-anchor verbs contain no mv.
